mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation and discount future cash flows more heavily, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same regime are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS for three consecutive months reduces the real discount rate, increasing the present value of expected corporate earnings and pushing S&P 500 forward returns positively over the next quarter (60 trading days).
failure_condition: Quarterly forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior quarter's average (p > 0.05), or the 3-month FEDFUNDS decline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in PAYEMS (labor market additions) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive in > 60% of triggered periods (binomial test p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not significant (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the HOUST (residential construction) index exceeds its 12-month moving average by at least 10%, it signals a rebound in domestic demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next month.
failure_condition: 30-day ahead returns in such periods are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the HOUST signal is not confirmed by other demand indicators (e.g., GDPC1 lagged growth < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) exceeding 5% for two months indicates weakening supply capacity, which raises the cost of capital and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (12-month moving average of INDPRO) - 5 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative in > 70% of such episodes (binomial test p < 0.05), or INDPRO decline is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI year-on-year) surprises strongly upward (> 1.5%) while FEDFUNDS remains below 1%, it suggests inflation expectations are rising faster than policy is tightening, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > (12-month moving average CPIAUCSL) + 1.5 and FEDFUNDS < 1
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in such episodes are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or the CPIAUCSL-FEDFUNDS interaction is not significant (Rank IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 3.5% accompanied by a sustained rise in PAYEMS (> 2% monthly for three months) indicates a labor market shift toward expansion, which boosts investor confidence and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5 and PAYEMS > (lag(PAYEMS) + 2) for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive in > 80% of such regimes (binomial test p < 0.05), or the UNRATE-PAYEMS interaction is not significant (Rank IC < 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in GDPC1 (GDP growth quarterly) below 2% for two consecutive quarters, with no offsetting strength in supply indicators (e.g., INDPRO), predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to elevated risk premia.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < 2 for two consecutive quarters and INDPRO < (12-month moving average INDPRO) - 1
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically negative in > 50% of such episodes (binomial test p > 0.05), or the GDPC1-INDPRO interaction is not significant (Rank IC > 0.1).
